title: Search Models and Querying
readerIntent: Understand how Nodics exposes searchable business data without coupling callers to one search engine.
priorKnowledge: Understand the purpose of a Nodics schema and item model.
summary: Search models describe searchable behavior and normalized operations; configured providers execute engine-specific indexing and queries.

sections.heading: Four different responsibilities
items: The owning business schema defines authoritative records and business rules.
A source-owned index definition declares what should be searchable.
The provider-neutral search model exposes normalized index and query operations.
A configured engine adapter translates those operations to an external engine.

sections.heading: Why this separation matters
paragraphs: Business modules should not contain Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, or Solr client calls. They declare searchable intent and call the shared search contract, allowing the engine to change without rewriting business callers.
